free_tier.stated: No free tier. MCI-N-B is EUR 1.25 a month: 1 shared vCPU, 1024 MiB RAM, 20 GB HDD, 10 Gbps fair-use bandwidth, one dedicated IPv6 address (/128), IPv6 only. A second rung, MCI-N-C, is EUR 1.25 a quarter for 384 MiB and 5 GB.

retention.stated: no retention statement is printed; the page instead carries 'No data safety guarantee - Please ensure your own backups'

egress.terms: 10 Gbps fair-use bandwidth with no byte allowance published

interface_detail: an instance with one dedicated IPv6 address as a /128; there is no IPv4 at all and no NAT layer, so every port on that single address is reachable and nothing else is.
tooling: any SSH client over IPv6; BGP is available up to 20 routes with downstream support after a ticket
chaining: 1 GiB for EUR 1.25 a month is the second-best shape per dollar, but a /128 rather than a prefix means the box has exactly one address to listen on

limits.value: one IPv6 /128 per instance; no prefix, so a second address needs an additional instance
'10 Gbps Fair Use bandwidth' with no byte figure and no published threshold

binding_note: a single /128 is the hard ceiling: there is no routed prefix, so anything needing more than one address needs another instance.

identity_cost.detail: an account on store.axivora.net (a register link exists); the form itself was not read. No card hold is stated on any page read. Payment rails were not read.

reliability_note: no reliability event observed; the vendor states 'No data safety guarantee - Please ensure your own backups'
confidence_note: shape, the /128 statement, the fair-use bandwidth line, the two prices and the billing periods are quoted from the vendor's product page read. The cart is the product page itself: the 'Order Now' button is an anchor to the same product path and the add-to-cart is a Livewire action, so there is no GET cart URL to give a buyer.

evidence.proved: quoted: 'MCI-N-B (IPv6 Only) Starting at €1.25 per month ... 1 Shared vCPU ... 1024 MiB RAM ... 20 GB HDD ... 10000 Mbps (10Gbps) Fair Use bandwidth ... IPv6-only environment' and 'MCI-N-C (IPv6 Only) Starting at €1.25 per quarter ... 384 MiB RAM ... 5 GB HDD'

quoted: 'Only IPv6 is supported; you cannot access any IPv4 internet.' and 'Each instance is assigned one dedicated IPv6 address (/128).' and 'No data safety guarantee - Please ensure your own backups'
quoted BGP terms: 'Up to 20 BGP routes with downstream support' and 'A ticket must be submitted to enable the BGP session.'
the cart page renders 'Your cart is empty' at 200, so the store is live; the add-to-cart itself is a Livewire wire:click action on the product page, not a link with a product id

notes: The best RAM-per-euro among the rows whose cart can be found, and the only one that states the delivery form outright: a single /128. That is enough for a WireGuard endpoint or a monitor (one address, every port open) but it is not a routed prefix, so the 'every port on the guest's own address' advantage stops at one address. The caveats stack: no data-safety guarantee, no published traffic ceiling, no published payment rails, and an entity that the store does not name on any page reached. Not established: who operates Axivora, the registration and checkout fields, payment rails, card hold, and whether 'per quarter' on MCI-N-C is the minimum term for MCI-N-B too.
